Maurice Ravel. A French composer, pianist and conductor widely regarded as one of France's greatest composers.

Often associated with Claude Debussy as a pioneer of Impressionist music, though both rejected the term, Ravel was a meticulous craftsman who combined traditional formal structures with novel harmonic language and brilliant orchestration. His work is celebrated for its lush textures, Spanish influence, and virtuosic piano writing.

Ravel's most famous and commercially successful work is Boléro, a one-movement orchestral piece from 1928 featuring an unchanging eighteen-bar melody repeated eighteen times in a gradual, massive crescendo over a relentless snare drum ostinato. Daphnis et Chloé, completed in 1912, is a massive, lush ballet commissioned by Sergei Diaghilev for the Ballets Russes, featuring a wordless chorus and widely considered Ravel's orchestral masterpiece.

La Valse, composed in 1920, is a choreographic poem conceived as an homage to the Viennese waltz. It features increasingly chaotic, swirling themes that are often interpreted as a metaphor for the destruction of pre-war European civilization.

Gaspard de la Nuit is a devilishly difficult three-movement piano suite from 1908, based on poems by Aloysius Bertrand. Its final movement, Scarbo, was deliberately written to be more technically demanding than Balakirev's Islamey. Pavane for a Dead Princess, from 1899, is a brief, wistful piece originally written for solo piano and later orchestrated, designed to evoke a slow court dance that a young Spanish princess might have danced.

Perhaps most remarkably, Ravel created what became the definitive orchestration of Modest Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition. Completed in 1922, this version cemented Ravel's reputation as a master orchestrator and became far more widely performed than the original piano suite. Along with Debussy, Ravel defined the French impressionistic sound world of the early twentieth century. He also had a deep appreciation for Russian music and worked on editing Mussorgsky's unfinished opera Khovanshchina alongside Igor Stravinsky.
